cloudEscalation.note: Cloud tier is strictly opt-in. While optIn is false, routing and fallback never select cloud hosts, even when all self-hosted tiers are unreachable. Set optIn to true or export XX_STACK_ALLOW_CLOUD=1 to enable cloud escalation.

rules.name: Prefer local for code execution
rules.when: editing, test execution, code review, short iterative loops

rules.name: Prefer local for orchestration and planning
rules.when: orchestration, planning, architecture framing, broad synthesis on the primary controller

rules.name: Use remote for delegated subagents
rules.when: parallel subagent reasoning, delegated research, overflow analysis, non-blocking long-context slices

rules.name: Escalate to cloud when justified and opted in
rules.when: cloud escalation is explicitly opted in AND required model capability is unavailable locally/remotely, latency is acceptable, or quality/availability requirements outweigh local cost savings

rules.name: Prefer OpenAI-compatible remote lane when enabled
rules.when: sglang, openai-compatible endpoint, llama-server, turboquant, llama.cpp preferred lane, localai fallback lane

rules.name: Prefer turboquant lane for long-context low-latency tasks
rules.when: long-context, low-latency, sufficient memory headroom, llama.cpp lane enabled

rules.name: Avoid turboquant lane for tool-critical tasks without validated support
rules.when: strict function-calling, strict json mode, tool reliability not validated

rules.name: Fallback behavior
rules.when: preferred tier is unavailable or overloaded

tiers.label: Self-hosted local Ollama
tiers.usageGuidance: Use first for fast coding, verification, and review loops on the current machine.

avoidTaskTypes: very-long-context synthesis when local GPUs are actively needed for development
concurrent multi-model workloads on the same Ollama endpoint unless explicitly proven safe

limits: Best for low-latency coding and iterative execution
Do not schedule too many concurrent heavy reasoning jobs if active development is in progress
If multiple slices require different Ollama models on this host, serialize them and switch models only at explicit handoff boundaries

hosts.label: Hermes local-first control plane (loopback proxy)
hosts.connectionNotes: OpenAI-compatible loopback proxy exposed by hermes-orchestration. Start it with `python3 hermes-orchestration/scripts/hermes_orchestrator.py serve` and export HERMES_PROXY_TOKEN. Hermes applies its own self-hosted-first lane policy behind this single endpoint, so routing here delegates lane selection to Hermes rather than picking a backend directly. Set enabled=true once the proxy is running; check readiness with `curl http://127.0.0.1:8180/healthz`.

avoidTaskTypes: work that must pin one specific backend

models.name: hermes-auto
models.notes: Virtual model name — Hermes selects the real backend per its own lane policy.

tiers.label: Tailscale Ollama compatibility lane
tiers.usageGuidance: Use for delegated subagents and parallel reasoning slices while local orchestration continues on the workstation. Currently backed by Skippy (8x RTX 5090 Debian rig); the sglang OpenAI-compatible lane is the preferred remote lane.

hosts.label: Skippy Debian AI rig (Ollama lane)
hosts.connectionNotes: Skippy (skippy-debian-5090, the MagicDNS name). Ollama is installed but currently refuses connections on the Tailscale interface; on Skippy set a systemd override with Environment="OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434" (or bind only to the tailnet address from `tailscale ip -4`) and restart ollama, then re-run setup to sync inventory and flip reachable.

limits: Primary remote lane runs sglang on :30000; keep Ollama as the compatibility lane
Prefer sglang lane for long-context and high-throughput work

tiers.label: Tailscale OpenAI-compatible lane
tiers.usageGuidance: Preferred remote lane: Skippy runs sglang (OpenAI-compatible /v1) on 8x RTX 5090s. Keep the Ollama lane available as compatibility fallback when tool or JSON reliability is not yet validated.

hosts.label: Skippy sglang endpoint (8x RTX 5090)
hosts.connectionNotes: Skippy (skippy-debian-5090, the MagicDNS name) running sglang on :30000. Serves qwen3-coder-next with a 262144-token context window.

hardware.summary: 8x RTX 5090 Debian AI rig (Skippy) running sglang

tiers.label: Cloud AI services
tiers.usageGuidance: Opt-in only: routing never falls back to this tier unless selectionPolicy.cloudEscalation.optIn is true (or XX_STACK_ALLOW_CLOUD=1). Use only when a hosted model or API is materially better for the task, or a workflow explicitly requires a cloud provider.

preferredTaskTypes: capability gaps not met by self-hosted models
avoidTaskTypes: sensitive work that does not require cloud

useWhen: A required model is not available on local or remote Ollama
The task requires a provider-specific capability
avoidWhen: Local or remote models can satisfy the task at comparable quality
The task involves sensitive local-only work and a cloud call is unnecessary

avoidTaskTypes: local-first workflows with no cloud requirement

useWhen: A Google-specific model capability is required
Multimodal reasoning is needed and self-hosted options are insufficient
avoidWhen: Self-hosted options are available and adequate
The workload is primarily coding with tight feedback loops
